title: Land pi's verified row and its validators in ticfac's capability matrix
description:
Write the pi row from the evidence tick gjk produced, and enforce it. gjk runs
the live round trip and lands NO config; this tick lands the config and the
validators, and needs the config split (wgi) first so the row sits beside the
roles and tiers tables once those are ticfac's.

Read gjk's RESULT file first. It answers, with commands and output: pi's real
unattended flag, whether pi silently substitutes an unknown model id, what the
effort suffix does on a model with no thinking dimension, and a completed round
trip with the echoed argv, agent_session, confirmed resume and integration
status. Do not re-derive any of that; if something is missing, say so rather
than guessing — the row's whole value is that it was run.

## Specifying WHICH pi model a tier uses, robustly

The mechanism already exists and needs no new syntax: a tier overlay may set
kind, model and effort together, exactly as the `balanced` tier does today for
codex (`.tick/runners.toml`). A pi tier is therefore:

    [roles.implement.tiers.economy]
    kind = "pi"
    model = "cloudflare-workers-ai/@cf/zai-org/glm-5.3-flash"
    effort = "low"

What is NOT robust is everything that decides whether that string means what it
says. Three specific problems, all in scope here:

1. THE SUBSTITUTION QUESTION, which is the whole of robustness. opencode was
   caught silently swallowing an unknown model id: `--model
   openai/gpt-9-imaginary` started green, answered the first-round-trip gate
   with a clean OK, and ran the entire turn on the CLI's own default, with only
   the pane footer betraying it (herdr-kinds.md, observed 2026-08-13). If pi
   does the same, a tier is decorative: the run reports the model it asked for
   and bills a different one. DETERMINE THIS EMPIRICALLY, first, with a
   deliberately bad id. The answer decides how strict the rest must be. Note
   `pi models` reports the session's current model in-band, which may be the
   read-back that catches a substitution.

2. VALIDATE AGAINST PI'S OWN CATALOG, not a regex. `providerQualified`
   (kinds.go:306) only asks whether a slash appears somewhere, so every typo
   passes. pi ships a real oracle: `pi --list-models` prints provider, model,
   context, max-out, THINKING and images (84 rows here), and `pi --list-models
   <search>` filters it and prints `No models matching "<x>"` for an unknown
   one. Use it. Note `pi auth check --model <nonsense>` reports ready — it
   validates the PROVIDER only and is NOT a model oracle; do not reach for it.
   Decide and log where the check runs: compile time is where a bad tier should
   die, but the catalog is a live command, so state what happens when pi is
   absent (refuse, or degrade to the shape check and say so).

3. THE THINKING DIMENSION IS PER-MODEL. The catalog's `thinking` column is
   yes/no per model, and pi's effort is appended as a SUFFIX (`model:high`)
   rather than a flag. Several cloudflare models are `no`. Appending a level to
   one of those is the same class of error opencode's row already refuses. Use
   the catalog column to decide, and follow that precedent: a tier that asks for
   an effort a model has no dimension for is a refusal naming the tier, the
   model and the column, not a silent drop.

The point of all three: a tier must mean the model it names, or refuse. A tier
that silently becomes something else is worse than no tier, because the run's
own provenance will attest to the model that was requested.

## What lands here

- The pi row with fullAuto set from gjk's evidence and fullAutoVerified true,
  and the pi section of the kinds reference written from that run.
- Model validation against pi's own catalog rather than the slash check, with
  the pi-absent behaviour a logged decision.
- A refusal for a bare id that names no provider.
- A refusal for an effort level on a model whose catalog thinking column is
  'no', matching the opencode precedent that a missing effort dimension is a
  refusal and not a silent drop.
- If gjk found that pi CAN substitute silently, the read-back that proves the
  model which ran is the model the tier named, and a refusal on mismatch.

acceptance_criteria: The pi row carries the full-auto template gjk verified, with its verified flag set, and the kinds reference's pi section is written from that run rather than re-derived. A tier's model id is validated against pi's own catalog (pi --list-models) rather than a slash check, so a typo dies at compile time; what happens when pi is absent is a logged decision. A bare id naming no provider is refused. An effort level on a model whose catalog thinking column is 'no' is refused naming the tier, the model and the column. If gjk found pi can substitute silently, a read-back proves the model that ran is the model the tier named and a mismatch is a refusal. Tests cover a good pi tier, a typo'd model, a bare unqualified id, and an effort on a non-thinking model. go test -short -timeout 45m ./... green (make test-short).
